newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends up on local bank activity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends up on local bank activity.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar reversed early falls to close higher against its American counterpart on Friday on active U.S. dollar sales by local banks, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.509, off a T$27.547 low, against Wednesday's T$27.538 close.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$286.5 million. The market was closed on Thursday for a national holiday.
"Several local banks turned active in selling U.S. dollars in afternoon trade, in part reflecting the (downward) correction on the U.S. dollar against the yen overseas," said one dealer.
The end of month-end U.S. dollar demand also helped the local unit's appreciation, she said.
Dealers said direction for the Taiwan dollar in the near term was not clear, although several of them expected a Taiwan dollar downtrend in the mid-term.
For Saturday, a T$27.50-27.52 range was seen.
